definition: An epileptogenic lesion is a focal brain abnormality associated with a person’s epilepsy. In this context, it serves as a reference point for examining how language functions are organized in the brain before and after epilepsy surgery.

reasons: The packet does not provide an explicit definition that an “epileptogenic lesion” is “a focal brain abnormality.” It only uses the term in the context of “focal lesional epilepsy” and analyzes language activations “with the epileptogenic lesion,” without stating the term’s meaning as a focal brain abnormality.

While the packet does support using the epileptogenic lesion as a reference point in analyses of “language representation” and language changes in relation to surgery (preoperative vs postoperative language fMRI/lateralization), the first substantive claim about the term’s definition is not supported by the provided text.
The packet does not define the term as a general concept; it uses ‘epileptogenic lesion’ only in the context of one study on children and young adults with focal lesional epilepsy.

The second sentence adds a study-specific role (‘reference point for examining how language functions are organized… before and after epilepsy surgery’) that is not a supported dictionary sense of the term.
The definition makes a broader causal claim about a ‘focal brain abnormality associated with a person’s epilepsy’ that is only indirectly suggested by the packet and not explicitly defined there.
